Deadline: Applications accepted from 1 September 2026; interviews 13 January – 31 March 2027; offers from 25 January 2027
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: IMGs in a US or Canadian residency must qualify for a CA medical licence, have completed a radiology residency (or 4 years postgraduate radiology training) and passed USMLE Steps I–III.
Application method: UCLA Recruit online application.
Licence requirement: Must qualify for a California medical licence prior to the start of fellowship.
Summary: A new one-year clinical fellowship concentrated in multi-modality cancer imaging (CT, MRI, PET/CT, PET/MR) with optional exposure to image-guided oncology procedures.

title: Pediatric Imaging Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiological Sciences, David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA (Pediatric Imaging, UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital)
Deadline: Applications accepted from 1 September 2026; interviews 11 January – 31 March 2027; offers from 25 January 2027
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: IMGs in a US or Canadian residency must have passed USMLE Steps I–III (not required for Medical Council of Canada licensees), have 4 years of ACGME/RCPSC-accredited postgraduate training and qualify for a CA medical licence.
Application method: UCLA Recruit online application.
Visa support: Must be US citizen/permanent resident or eligible for an ECFMG-sponsored J-1 visa (reviewed by the GME Dean's office).
Licence requirement: Must qualify for a California medical licence prior to the start of fellowship.
Summary: The one-year ACGME-approved pediatric imaging position exposes the fellow to a variety of practice settings and the full scope of pediatric imaging modalities.

title: Independent Interventional Radiology Residency
Department: Department of Radiological Sciences, David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA (Interventional Radiology)
Deadline: ERAS December cycle; applications can be submitted from 13 November 2026
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: IMGs in a US or Canadian residency must have passed USMLE Steps I–III (not required for Medical Council of Canada licensees), have 4 years of ACGME/RCPSC-accredited postgraduate training and qualify for a CA medical licence.
Application method: ERAS; participates in the NRMP Match.
Visa support: Must be US citizen/permanent resident or eligible for an ECFMG-sponsored J-1 visa (reviewed by the GME Dean's office).
Licence requirement: Must qualify for a California medical licence prior to the start of fellowship.
Summary: UCLA's ACGME-accredited Independent IR Residency provides dedicated interventional radiology training after diagnostic radiology residency, recruited through ERAS and the NRMP.

title: Body Imaging Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Abdominal Imaging)
Duration: 1 year (8 months UCSF CT/MR, 2 months ultrasound, 2 months ZSFG)
Start: Openings for the 2026–2027 and 2027–2028 fellowship years
Eligibility: Completion of a four-year diagnostic radiology residency from an accredited program.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: UCSF online fellowship application (CV, personal statement, headshot, USMLE/COMLEX scores, three letters of recommendation including one from current program director). Does not participate in the NRMP Match.
Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: The UCSF Body Imaging fellowship provides comprehensive and structured training in all aspects of abdominal and pelvic imaging, maximising learning in advanced multimodality imaging using MRI, CT, PET and ultrasound.

title: Breast Imaging Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Breast Imaging)
Eligibility: Completion of a four-year diagnostic radiology residency from an accredited program.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: FellowshipCAS; participates in the SBI Breast Imaging Fellowship Match (NRMP); virtual interviews 11 January – 31 March 2027.
Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: UCSF offers one-year breast imaging fellowship positions at Mission Bay and the ZSFG Avon Comprehensive Breast Care Center covering mammography, tomosynthesis, ultrasound, MRI and interventional procedures.

title: Cardiothoracic Imaging Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Cardiothoracic Imaging)
Eligibility: Completion of a four-year diagnostic radiology residency from an accredited program.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: UCSF online fellowship application (CV, personal statement, headshot, USMLE/COMLEX scores, three letters of recommendation including one from current program director). Does not participate in the NRMP Match.
Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: The cardiothoracic imaging fellowship trains radiologists in all aspects of clinical thoracic imaging including cardiovascular MRI/MRA, coronary CT angiography, chest CT, high-resolution CT and biopsy techniques.

title: Musculoskeletal Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Musculoskeletal Imaging)
Start: 2028–2029 (online application, per SCARD timeline opening 1 September)
Eligibility: Completion of a four-year diagnostic radiology residency from an accredited program.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: UCSF online fellowship application (CV, personal statement, headshot, USMLE/COMLEX scores, three letters of recommendation including one from current program director). Participates in the NRMP Match.
Positions: 5 selected each year (fellowships page lists 6 positions)
Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: The one-year clinical musculoskeletal fellowship at UCSF encompasses all aspects of the musculoskeletal division, with rotations at Parnassus and the UCSF Orthopaedic Institute at Mission Bay and a significant volume of MSK interventions.

title: Neurointerventional Radiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Neuroendovascular Surgery)
Eligibility: Radiology applicants: diagnostic radiology residency plus twelve months of diagnostic neuroradiology training. Neurosurgery/neurology applicants: completed residency and board eligible; neurology applicants must complete a vascular neurology fellowship first.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: UCSF online application; rolling applications; does not participate in the NRMP Match.
Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: The Neurointerventional Radiology fellowship provides extensive training in diagnostic and interventional neuroradiology as well as intensive care unit medicine under the supervision of full-time faculty.

title: Pediatric Radiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Pediatric Radiology, UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals)
Eligibility: Completion of a four-year diagnostic radiology residency from an accredited program.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: UCSF online fellowship application (CV, personal statement, headshot, USMLE/COMLEX scores, three letters of recommendation including one from current program director). Does not participate in the NRMP Match.
Visa support: The University sponsors J-1 ECFMG visas for fellowship positions in the majority of cases.
Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: The pediatric radiology fellowship at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital provides comprehensive training centred on the Mission Bay campus, with additional rotation time at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital Oakland.

title: Nuclear Medicine Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Molecular Imaging and Therapeutics Division)
Eligibility: Completion of diagnostic radiology residency.
International applicants: Graduates of medical schools outside the US or Canada must hold a valid ECFMG certificate at the time of application, be eligible for a California Medical License and have passed USMLE Steps I, II and III (or COMLEX/LMCC equivalent).
Application method: UCSF online fellowship application (CV, personal statement, headshot, USMLE/COMLEX scores, three letters of recommendation including one from current program director). Does not participate in the NRMP Match.

Licence requirement: Radiology board certification (or board eligibility) and a California Medical License are required prior to appointment.
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited nuclear medicine fellowship offered by the Molecular Imaging and Therapeutics Division for those who have completed diagnostic radiology residency.

title: Independent Interventional Radiology Residency
Department: Department of Radiology and Biomedical Imaging, UCSF (Interventional Radiology)
Start: After completion of PGY-5 DR year
Eligibility: Diagnostic radiology residents (apply in PGY-4); ESIR and non-ESIR tracks.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: ERAS ACGME Fellowship December cycle (applications from 1 November); all positions filled through the NRMP.
Positions: Up to 4 per year (fellowships page lists 3 positions)
Summary: The Independent IR residency replaces the IR fellowship as the route to subspecialised IR training after diagnostic radiology residency, with rotations across three UCSF campuses, vascular surgery and IR clinic.

title: Abdominal Radiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine (Abdominal Imaging)
Deadline: 2028–2029 applications accepted from 1 September 2026 (SCARD embargo; virtual interviews)
Eligibility: Radiologists who have completed residency training in diagnostic radiology.
International applicants: International graduates submit USMLE Steps 1, 2-CK and 3, ECFMG certificate, residency completion documentation and home-country board certification.
Application method: Email PDF application (CV, personal statement, USMLE scores, letters) to fellowbi@uw.edu.
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship in abdominal imaging, established in 1979, covering diagnostic ultrasound, CT, MR and imaging-guided interventions across four sites.

title: Breast Imaging Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine (Breast Imaging Section, Fred Hutch Cancer Center)
Eligibility: Radiology board certification or eligibility.
International applicants: Foreign applicants require an approved work visa.
Application method: FellowshipsCAS only; SBI Breast Imaging Match via NRMP (All In policy).
Summary: A 12-month fellowship at the Fred Hutch Cancer Center offering comprehensive training in all aspects of breast imaging.

title: Cancer Imaging Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME, AOA, ACGME-I Advanced Specialty, RCPSC or CFPC-accredited residency and all USMLE steps; or an international DR residency with home-country DR board certification.
International applicants: International graduates accepted with home-country diagnostic radiology board certification; participates in the department's ABR alternate pathway programme.
Application method: Rolling, first-come first-accepted admissions; no Match.
Visa support: Committed to supporting international applicants by sponsoring visas.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible to obtain a State of Washington medical license.
Summary: A one-year non-ACGME fellowship providing in-depth experience in oncologic imaging across MRI, CT, ultrasound, PET-CT, PET-MRI and image-guided procedures, with six months each in abdominal imaging and nuclear medicine.

title: Cardiothoracic Radiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine (Cardiothoracic Imaging)
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited radiology residency in the US or RCPSC-accredited program in Canada (or equivalent radiology residency in another country with ECFMG certification); preference for ABR-certified or eligible candidates.
International applicants: Equivalent residency in another country accepted with ECFMG certification.
Application method: Email application form and documents to the Program Administrator.
Visa support: Eligible for new J-1 sponsorship; ineligible for new H-1B sponsorship; H-1B and J-1 transfers supported.
Summary: A non-ACGME cardiothoracic radiology fellowship, founded in 2009, with hands-on training in cardiac and thoracic radiographs, CT and MR.

title: Emergency Radiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine (Emergency Radiology)
Deadline: Applications accepted from 1 September (SCARD embargo; ASER dates)
Eligibility: Completion of a radiology residency and USMLE Step 3 passed before the start of fellowship.
International applicants: An alternate four-year ABR pathway is available for international medical graduates.
Application method: Downloadable application form; interviews via Zoom.
Summary: A non-ACGME emergency radiology fellowship in a multi-site setting including major trauma and referral centres, with state-of-the-art trauma and emergency imaging.

title: Musculoskeletal Radiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine (Musculoskeletal Radiology)
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited radiology residency in the US or RCPSC-accredited program in Canada (or equivalent radiology residency in another country with ECFMG certification); preference for ABR-certified or eligible candidates. Must be in the ABR certification process by fellowship start.
International applicants: Equivalent residency in another country accepted with ECFMG certification.
Application method: SSR MSK Fellowship Common Application emailed to Program Administrator; interviews via RezRate; NRMP Match (program code 1918R26F0).
Licence requirement: Able to obtain an unrestricted Washington State medical licence by 1 July 2028.
Summary: A 12-month non-ACGME musculoskeletal fellowship, founded in 1992, with advanced hands-on clinical training in MSK diagnostic imaging and procedures including sports medicine, tumour and orthopaedic trauma cases.

title: Neuroradiology Fellowship
Department: Department of Radiology, University of Washington School of Medicine (Neuroradiology)
Eligibility: Completed diagnostic radiology residency and USMLE Step 3; board eligible or certified in diagnostic radiology.
International applicants: Trains local, national and international applicants; alternate four-year ABR pathway available for IMGs.
Application method: ERAS and NRMP Match; if unfilled, applications by email outside the Match.
Funding: First-year stipend (R6) $98,160 for FY 2026–2027; medical/dental and malpractice coverage; four weeks paid vacation.
Visa support: Foreign nationals appointed on J1 visa status unless special circumstances; existing H1 visas may be extended with GME/ISO approval.
Licence requirement: Must have applied for a Washington State medical license before the start of fellowship.
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited neuroradiology fellowship providing comprehensive experience in all aspects of neuroradiology, with an optional non-ACGME second year.

title: Pediatric Radiology Fellowship
